old.name: The Rum (Greek) Quarter
old.hook: Narrow lanes and bougainvillea-draped stone houses below the bell tower.
old.text: Narrow lanes and bougainvillea-draped stone houses below the bell tower. The living trace of a Greek community that once numbered close to 2,000 and now counts about twenty, most having left amid 20th-century state pressure. The restored guesthouses, galleries and wine bars cluster here. A walking quarter, not a ticket · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Bozcaada Castle (Tenedos Fortress)
old.hook: The harbour fortress rebuilt for Mehmet II in 1455 over Phoenician, Venetian and Genoese foundations.
old.text: The harbour fortress rebuilt for Mehmet II in 1455 over Phoenician, Venetian and Genoese foundations. A waterside stronghold of bailey, citadel and dry landward moat guarding the strait. Walk the ramparts for the town-and-harbour view; it is floodlit after dark. Earlier works on the site were demolished after the 14th-century War of Chioggia between Venice and Genoa. Modest ticket; the harbour-view walk · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Church of St Mary — Kimisis Theotokou
old.hook: The island's last working Greek Orthodox church, built 1869 in the Rum quarter.
old.text: The island's last working Greek Orthodox church, built 1869 in the Rum quarter. A three-aisled nave divided by five Corinthian-capitalled columns, under a four-storey bell tower of 1895 visible from almost anywhere in town — the standing heart of a community that has all but gone. Active church; respect services · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Bozcaada Local History Museum
old.hook: A private island museum, opened 2005 by the collector Hakan Gürüney.
old.text: A private island museum, opened 2005 by the collector Hakan Gürüney. Fossils, archaeological pieces, coins, maps, old island wine bottles and Greek-and-Turkish household goods gathered into a central historic building — an hour out of the wind, and the quickest way to read the island's layers. Modest admission; central · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: The Stone Windmills (Yel Değirmenleri)
old.hook: Cylindrical stone windmills on the high ground that once ground the island's wheat.
old.text: Cylindrical stone windmills on the high ground that once ground the island's wheat. Bozcaada had about a dozen; most fell to ruin as mechanical mills took over, and three were rebuilt in 2019 with domed roofs and white sail-frames — a 10–15 minute walk up from town for a view back over castle and harbour. Free; a short uphill walk · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Ayazma Monastery & Holy Spring
old.hook: A modest Greek Orthodox chapel under plane trees beside a twin-spouted holy spring, near Ayazma beach.
old.text: A modest Greek Orthodox chapel under plane trees beside a twin-spouted holy spring, near Ayazma beach. Closed for most of the year, it opens for the 26 July (Aya Paraskevi) pilgrimage — the spring that gives the beach its name. A shaded, cool counterpoint to the bare western cape. Mostly closed; opens 26 July · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Göztepe — the panorama
old.hook: The island's highest point at 192 m, on foot only — about half an hour gently up from the centre.
old.text: The island's highest point at 192 m, on foot only — about half an hour gently up from the centre. You cannot drive up; the payoff is a genuine 360-degree sweep over vineyards, pine, the windmills and the offshore islets. Go for sunrise or late afternoon, not midday. ~30 min up, on foot only · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: The vineyard country
old.hook: Vines cover much of the interior — the island's defining inland walk, gentle open country between Göztepe and the south coast.
old.text: Vines cover much of the interior — the island's defining inland walk, gentle open country between Göztepe and the south coast. The respected producers are Corvus, Talay, Çamlıbağ (Yunatçılar) and Ataol; several can be tasted in town, but the walk between the rows is the point. Open country; carry water · Open in Google Maps →
